Home screen, dock, tabs, poisons, blocks and settings, in a file
Replaces everything with a saved file; blocks are only added
Replaces the home screen, dock, tabs and settings, and adds the blocks you lack: it never removes or changes one. Missing widgets are set up again by tapping them.

Replaces the home screen, dock, tabs, hidden apps and grids; poisons, the app the pause offers, vibration, the number format, how paused apps show and whether the dock and the search bar show stay. Widgets are set up again by tapping them.

Shortcut already on the home screen or dock
Everything you can do, part by part
This is what Islauncher can do, part by part. To read it again: long-press an empty spot on the home screen → Settings → Guide.
Long-press an icon or widget and drag it; hold it at a side of the screen to change page
Long-press it → Remove. Or throw it: drag it and let go with a quick flick; Undo brings it back
Long-press an app on the home screen, in the dock or in the drawer: its shortcuts come first, and + puts one on the home screen
Long-press it → Rename; the drawer and search keep the app\'s name
With more than one page, long-press an item → Move to another page; it keeps its spot there if that is free
Long-press an app on the home screen or in the drawer → Uninstall; Android asks first, and its icons go with it. Uninstalled another way (App info, as from the dock), its icons stay for Tidy up
Long-press an empty spot: Add widget, Wallpaper or Settings
In Settings → Home screen, add, reorder and remove pages and pick the main one; a removed page\'s items move to the others
In Settings → Home screen; a smaller grid deletes nothing, it moves what no longer fits
Lists what is broken, duplicated or empty, each with its own Remove; nothing goes by itself
Apps paused by Focus mode or Digital Wellbeing are greyed out; Settings → Home screen can hide them instead
When an app, such as a browser, adds a shortcut to the home screen, Islauncher asks you first. If the pages are full, it adds a page
Long-press an empty spot → Add widget; search by app or name, with each one\'s preview and size
Long-press a widget → Resize, then drag the dots on its sides; tap outside when done
Long-press a widget → Set up again, then tap it: its setup screen opens again, unless it has none or its setup is optional
After a Nova import, or restoring a backup whose widgets are gone, tap each + widget to set it up
Long-press a dock icon → Configure: what a tap and a swipe up or down on it open
Drag an app from the drawer or the home screen onto an empty spot in the dock
Settings → Dock → Show dock: turned off, the home screen takes its space and the dock\'s icons stay saved

Add, reorder and remove dock pages and set the icons per page in Settings → Dock; swipe the dock sideways between pages, and with Infinite scroll the last leads to the first. The house marks the main page: the dock starts there and goes back to it after you open an app
Swipe up on the home screen; to close it, pull down from the top of the list

Installed WebAPKs and accepted browser web shortcuts appear in the drawer and search; new ones are also added to Home, once. Removing a Home icon keeps it in the drawer; Delete shortcut, in a web shortcut\'s menu, removes it everywhere. Shortcuts pinned by another launcher may need adding again from the browser
Its columns, and how many rows fit on one screen, in Settings → App drawer
Swipe sideways from one to the next; long-press one to rename it, add a tab, or delete a tab of picked apps
Settings → App drawer → the tab → Choose apps, or tick its tabs in an app\'s menu; a new tab takes its apps out of All apps tabs (such as Apps) until you turn off Hide its apps from All apps there
Long-press it → Hide from drawer; search still finds it
Long-press an app → Add to home screen, or drag it onto the home screen or the dock
Drag the bar on the right edge of the list

resources.string: Pick a healthy app in Settings → App drawer: the pause offers it, with no wait
Every open through Islauncher: icons, dock, gestures, shortcuts and search; not notifications or Recents
Anywhere on the home screen, except on a dock icon with a swipe of its own, it opens the app drawer
Anywhere on the home screen, except on a dock icon with a swipe of its own, it opens the notifications
Tap an empty spot twice to open the app you pick in Settings → Gestures
Closes whatever is open: a menu, the drawer or Settings. With nothing open on the home screen, it goes to the main page, and on the main page it opens search
A light vibration on long presses, drops, throws, swipes, the double tap, each step of a widget\'s resize and settings controls; you can turn it off in Settings → Gestures
Long-press an empty spot on the home screen, or the search bar → Settings
Settings → Home app: pick Islauncher, so the Home button opens it; only then do an app\'s shortcuts and shortcuts from other apps work
Save the home screen, dock, tabs, settings and blocks to a file and restore them later (a restore only adds the blocks you lack); after a reinstall, add home screen shortcuts again from their app
A new copy each week in a folder you choose; the old ones stay
Brings the home screen, dock, tabs, hidden apps and grids from a .novabackup file
Islauncher has no network permission, so it cannot send anything; backups are saved on the phone
Apps and sites on a schedule
Keeps blocked apps and sites closed during their hours. It reads only which app is in front and a browser\'s address bar; it keeps none of it, and Islauncher has no network permission.
Islauncher will no longer keep itself from being uninstalled, and its blocks can be undone that way.
This browser\'s address can\'t be read: blocked until %s

During its hours a block keeps its apps from opening and its sites from showing in any browser, snoozes their notifications until it ends and pauses their sound. While it runs it can only grow: it can\'t be removed or shortened.
Missing: tap to turn it on
Optional: run scripts/blocks-setup.sh with USB debugging enabled, or tap to copy the commands. Blocks do not require this step. No account is removed.
Keeps Islauncher from being uninstalled while its blocks run. It asks for no other power over the phone.

The accessibility service can see the screen and notification access every notification. Islauncher uses only the app in front, a browser\'s address bar and a notification\'s app; it keeps none of it and has no network permission.
Its address bar was read on %s: sites are blocked one by one
Not read yet: if its address bar can\'t be read, it is blocked whole during blocks with sites
Removes device admin. Without ADB, turn accessibility off in the Android screen that opens, then turn notification access off in its setup row.
Running until %s: things can only be added
It can\'t be removed while the block runs
Blocks the site and its subdomains in any browser. Pages shown inside other apps are not covered: block those apps.
Not a site: write it like youtube.com
Choose at least one app or site
Each range needs a day, and a start and an end that differ
Leave at least an hour in a row free each week: a block that never ends could only go with a factory reset
It is running: until it ends it can only grow
It can be removed once it ends: %s
Its apps and sites can be used again.

Settings → Blocks: follow the three access steps on the phone, then choose apps, sites and hours: as many ranges as you need, and a chart of the week shows what they cover. ADB is optional for additional protection

It can only grow. Its apps go home whatever opens them, its sites go back in any browser, their notifications wait until it ends, their sound pauses, and the settings that would undo it are out of reach
Pages shown inside other apps, adb from a computer, a factory reset, and anything outside its hours, when it can be removed
Complete these three steps in order. Tap each missing access, enable Islauncher in Android, then return here. The status updates when you return.
Setup complete. You can now add blocks without a computer.
Open App info, then the menu at the top → Allow restricted settings, and confirm. Return here and retry the missing step. This option only appears when Android restricts a sideloaded app.
Blocks work without ADB. If you disable accessibility, Islauncher cannot turn it back on automatically or enforce automatic date and time during a block. Android may still let you stop the service.
Additional protection enabled: Islauncher can restore accessibility and keep date and time automatic during blocks.
